diocese: The Episcopal Diocese of San Joaquin
sourceFile: "dioceasn cycle of prayer 2026.docx" [sic, source's own filename typo], provided directly by Josh via Google Drive (file id 13OwPvF9Uhr1hZqwk1D3-c1xPh8eUZv0E, folder "TEC Cycle of Prayer").
notes: Self-contained calendar-year 2026 cycle, Jan 4 - Dec 27 (52 weeks). The source's own header warns 'this might have changes throughout the year' -- several individual weeks also carry their own '(this may change)' parenthetical, preserved verbatim on those subjects rather than stripped.

TWO DATE ERRORS FOUND AND CORRECTED, same method as episcopal-idaho-2026.json's (batch 2): the source's weekly dates otherwise form an unbroken Sunday sequence anchored on the confirmed Sunday Jan 4, 2026 (...Sep 6, 13, 20, [next]...; ...Oct 4, [next], 18, 25...). 'September 28 -- Holy Trinity...' breaks that sequence (28 is a Monday) and is corrected here to **September 27**. 'October 12 -- St Francis...' likewise breaks the sequence (12 is a Monday) and is corrected here to **October 11**. Both are checkable against the confirmed Sunday anchor, not guesses.

Each week's clergy/lay-leader description is folded into that week's own `parish` subject as its `note` field, per the source's own single-sentence phrasing ('St X in City, and their priest, the Rev. Y') rather than split into a separate `category` subject -- matching this session's own working decision for this diocese specifically (distinct from Great Lakes/Kentucky's own convention, where a subject's note is a short title, not a full clause). The source's own leading 'and'/connector before the clergy clause is trimmed from each `note` (e.g. printed 'and their priest, the Rev. Bob Woods' becomes note 'their priest, the Rev. Bob Woods') since it reads as a dangling conjunction once separated into its own field -- no name, title, or fact is altered by this trim, only the connective word joining it to the parish name.

Several weeks (diocesan leadership, commissions, seminarians, Retired Priests, the bishop transition) name no specific parish at all -- recorded as `category` subjects, their `name` the source's own sentence verbatim.

The diocese's own bishop changed mid-year: January 11 and July 19/26 name 'Bishop David Rice, our Bishop' vs. 'The Rt Rev Greg Kimura, our Bishop' -- both are the source's own real, different wording for different weeks (April 19's own entry is 'The ordination, consecration and installation of our new Bishop, The Rt. Rev. Greg Kimura'), not a transcription inconsistency.

Two source typos preserved verbatim, per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a diocese's own published document: 'Ms Cindy Smmith' (July 12, evidently 'Smith') and 'Ant-Racism' (December 13, evidently 'Anti-Racism' -- notably the source itself spells it correctly, 'Anti-Racism Commission', on June 14, so this is a one-off typo, not the diocese's own preferred spelling).
A trailing comma after November 8's clergy clause ('...the Rev. Christian Hagan,') is dropped as a plain punctuation/extraction artifact, not a content change.
